```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(readr)
dataset <- read_csv("dataset.csv")
library(ggplot2)
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r cars}
dataset <- dataset[, !names(dataset) %in% c("track_id", "artists", "album_name",
                                            "track_name", "explicit", "mode",
                                            "...1")]
colnames(dataset)
```

## Including Plots

Generated scatter plots for instrumentalness, liveness, valence, tempo, and 
track_genre as independent variables and popularity as the variable of interest.

```{r}
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = instrumentalness, y = popularity)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.05, width = 0.01, height = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Popularity vs Instrumentalness",
    x = "Instrumentalness",
    y = "Popularity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

```{r}
head(dataset)
#plot(dataset$tempo, dataset$popularity,
     #main="My Title",
     #xlab="tempo",
     #ylab="popularity")
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = tempo, y = popularity)) + # Changed to tempo
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.05, width = 0.01, height = 0.5) +
  # Ruler for Tempo (usually 50 to 200 BPM)
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 250, by = 25)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Popularity vs Tempo",
    x = "Tempo",
    y = "Popularity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = instrumentalness, y = popularity)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.05, width = 0.01, height = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Popularity vs valence",
    x = "valence",
    y = "Popularity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```




Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
